pr.title: [mir-opt] GVN some more transmute cases
pr.description:
We already did `Transmute`-then-`PtrToPtr`; this adds the nearly-identical `PtrToPtr`-then-`Transmute`.

It also adds `transmute(Foo(x))` → `transmute(x)`, when `Foo` is a single-field transparent type.  That's useful for things like `NonNull { pointer: p }.as_ptr()`.  It also detects when a `Transmute` is just an identity-for-the-value `PtrCast` between different raw pointer types, to help such things fold with other GVN passes.

Found these as I was looking at <https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-team/issues/807>-related changes.  This also removes the questionably-useful "turn a transmute into a field projection" part of instsimplify (which I added ages ago without an obvious need for it) since that would just put back the field projections that MCP807 is trying to ban.

r? mir-opt
pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason: The PR is an optimization/cleanup, not a semantic bug fix. The historical GVN behavior was non-application (leaving `Transmute` chains, aggregate wrappers, or `PtrToPtr` pairs intact), while the new behavior folds them into equivalent `PtrToPtr`/`Transmute`/field uses under metadata, variant, and niche guards. Likewise, InstSimplify's removed rewrite `transmute::<TransparentAdt, FieldTy>(v)` -> `v.field` is value-equivalent for valid `#[repr(transparent)]` structs/unions. Its removal is motivated by MCP#807 banning projections into `#[rustc_layout_scalar_valid_range_*]` types, not by an observable miscompile. Concrete valid inputs such as `transmute(Wrapping(-7_i16))` versus `.0`, `transmute(MyId(id))` versus `id`, or raw-pointer transmute versus pointer cast produce identical values. Any input that could expose a difference would require an invalid niche/scalar-valid-range value or other UB, which Miri rejects and which cannot serve as a defined counterexample. Since `test_program_pair` requires repeated defined O0/O3/Miri executions with different original/transformed results, no source-grounded pair exists for this PR without manufacturing an unrelated semantic change.

analysis.originalLogic: GVN's `simplify_cast` handled a few cast-chain cases in a single bounded pass: it stripped a `PtrToPtr` that casts away slice metadata from `AggregateTy::RawPtr`, collapsed `PtrToPtr`-then-`PtrToPtr`, and used one inner metadata check for the existing `PtrToPtr`/`Transmute` case. InstSimplify separately rewrote a `Transmute` from a transparent struct/union to a field projection when a field type exactly matched the cast type.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: For GVN, the historical behavior was limited/non-application rather than a semantic miscompile: it did not recognize a raw-pointer `Transmute` with equal metadata as a `PtrToPtr`, did not skip a single-field aggregate before `Transmute`, and did not iterate cast-chain rewrites to a fixed point. For InstSimplify, the removed historical transformation was `transmute(transparent ADT value)` -> projection to a matching field, shown in the old test as `_3 = move (_4.0: i16);` instead of `_3 = move _4 as i16 (Transmute);`; this is value-equivalent on the tested inputs but reintroduces projections that MCP#807 aims to ban.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR `Rvalue::Cast` chains using `CastKind::Transmute` and `PtrToPtr`; thin and fat raw pointers with equal or different metadata; `Aggregate` values from transparent single-field structs, one-payload enums, one-element tuples/arrays, and scalar/pointer aggregates; types with backend-relevant niches (`char`, `NonZero`, scalar-valid-range types) versus always-valid scalars; InstSimplify inputs involving transparent structs/unions cast to a field type.
analysis.summary: Historical optimization PR extending GVN transmute/cast simplification: raw-pointer transmutes become pointer casts when metadata matches, single-field aggregates can be skipped before transmute, cast chains are folded to a fixed point with metadata and niche guards, and InstSimplify no longer turns transparent-ADT transmutes into field projections. This is optimization knowledge, not a demonstrated bug fix; no compiler was built or executed.
analysis.trigger: GVN visits a cast whose operand resolves to an aggregate or another cast, or a `Transmute` between raw pointers with identical metadata. InstSimplify visits a transmute from a transparent ADT to a field type.
preconditions: A raw-pointer `Transmute` can become `PtrToPtr` only when `from.is_unsafe_ptr()`, `to.is_unsafe_ptr()`, and `self.pointers_have_same_metadata(from, to)` all hold.
Aggregate-then-transmute simplification requires a single-field value: either `layout.non_1zst_field(...)` with `layout.size == field_layout.size`, or a transparent struct with exactly one field.
The enum variant must be checked: `abi::Variants::Single { index }` must match the aggregate's variant, because the tag field is not present in the aggregate's field values.
If extracting the field reaches the target type directly (`field_ty == to`), GVN returns the field value; otherwise it continues folding the remaining cast chain.
Combining `Transmute`-then-`Transmute` is allowed only when the intermediate type has no niche of interest to the backend: `!self.type_may_have_niche_of_interest_to_backend(inner_to)`.

Combining `PtrToPtr`-then-`Transmute` requires same metadata between the inner cast's `inner_from` and `inner_to`; combining `Transmute`-then-`PtrToPtr` requires same metadata between the outer `from` and `to`.
Fat-to-thin pointer casts must not be merged with a transmute; the test states: `This cast is fat-to-thin, so can't be merged with the transmute`.
InstSimplify must not replace such transmutes with field projections, because projections into `[rustc_layout_scalar_valid_range_*]` types are banned by MCP#807.
pitfalls: Do not turn a raw-pointer `Transmute` into `PtrToPtr` when pointer metadata differs or the cast changes fat-to-thin representation.
Do not extract a field from an aggregate with multiple non-ZST fields, unequal layout size, or an enum tag; `Option<u16>` transmuted to `u32` still needs its tag and must retain the `Transmute`.
Do not skip an intermediate niche-bearing type such as `i32 -> char -> u32`; the backend needs those `assume`s, and the patch explicitly preserves them.
Do not treat every one-field type as safely collapsible: the code checks `non_1zst_field` and `layout.size == field_layout.size`, with a separate transparent-single-field-struct case.
Do not assume the old GVN loop already reached a fixed point; the PR replaces the bounded `was_updated` logic with an iterative `loop` so newly exposed cases can fold further.
Do not revive InstSimplify's transparent-ADT-to-field rewrite merely because the tested values are equivalent; it is specifically undesirable for scalar-valid-range layouts.
The PR is an optimization/cleanup, not a confirmed semantic miscompile; paired programs should test which MIR rewrite fires, not claim observable misbehavior.
analysis.testStrategy: Use MIR-dump regression tests that compare the same function before and after the pass, with `CHECK` patterns for the intended cast kind and operand. Cover positive cases: `transmute` between thin raw pointers of different mutability/pointee type, `transmute(Foo(x))` for a transparent single-field struct, single-payload enum, `(u16,)`, `[u16; 1]`, and `aggregate_raw_ptr`; assert the aggregate disappears and GVN emits `copy _1`/`copy _2` or a remaining `Transmute` only when needed. Cover negative/guard cases: fat-to-thin `*const [i32] -> *const i32`, `Option<u16> -> u32`, `Pair(u16,u16) -> u32`, and niche chains such as `u32 -> char -> i32`; assert the expected intermediate remains. For the InstSimplify change, use a transparent `Wrapping<i16>` and a scalar-valid-range type such as `#[rustc_layout_scalar_valid_range_end(55555)] struct MyId(u16);`, then assert with `CHECK-NOT` that no field projection was introduced and the `as i16 (Transmute)` remains. Include both panic-abort and panic-unwind MIR variants where the harness provides them.
evidence: We already did `Transmute`-then-`PtrToPtr`; this adds the nearly-identical `PtrToPtr`-then-`Transmute`.
It also adds `transmute(Foo(x))` → `transmute(x)`, when `Foo` is a single-field transparent type.
It also detects when a `Transmute` is just an identity-for-the-value `PtrCast` between different raw pointer types, to help such things fold with other GVN passes.
This also removes the questionably-useful "turn a transmute into a field projection" part of instsimplify
// Transmuting between raw pointers is just a pointer cast so long as
// Aggregate-then-Transmute can just transmute the original field value,
The backend will emit `assume`s when transmuting between types with niches,
// We needed to check the variant to avoid trying to read the tag
// This cast is fat-to-thin, so can't be merged with the transmute
// Transmutes should not be converted to field accesses, because MCP#807
